_comment: R8.3 / SG40 / R8.4 -- the chapter's climax, as data. This file owns the three things the stronghold's ROUTE (R8.2, data/config/stronghold.json) deliberately does not: who stands in the Warden Arena, where the reveal is delivered from, and what the freed legendary is. ALL NUMBERS TUNABLE per CLAUDE.md.
_comment_seam: R8.2/SG38's route was built by a sibling agent in parallel with this item. NOTHING here invents a second stronghold: every `mark` named below is one of the five `marks` that file already registers (warden_stand, warden_challenge, reveal_stand, machine_foot, legendary_stand), resolved at runtime through `scripts/world/stronghold.gd::marker()`, and the trainer group is its own `placed_by` convention. `fallback` on each entry is world metres [x, z] used ONLY when no stronghold node is in the tree -- a bare test scene, or this branch before the route merges -- so smoke_boss can drive the whole climax without depending on somebody else's building existing yet. When both exist the marker wins, always.

site._comment: The stronghold node this climax attaches itself to, by node name under the world. Nothing else about the building is assumed.
site.fallback_comment: The Warden Arena's own world box per stronghold.json is x[219,245] z[-227.4,-203.4] and the Legendary Chamber's is x[218,246] z[-197.4,-169.4]. These fallbacks are points inside those boxes, so a merged build and an unmerged one put the climax in the same place to within a couple of metres. They are a safety net, not a second layout.

_comment_reveal: SG40, spec Act VI step 33 ('environmental/story reveal') and Sec32's top rung. It is delivered by a Team Tether READOUT bolted to the arena's threshold -- the sibling's `warden_challenge` mark, which is the spot the player is stopped at on the way in -- so the reveal is environmental storytelling the player chooses to read, and it lands BEFORE the Warden speaks and before the fight, which is the order Sec28 makes non-optional. Nothing outside data/dialogue/stronghold.json may say these words; tests/test_dialogue_runner.gd fails the build if anything does.
_comment_duty_board: R-2 (docs/specs/GATE3_ENCOUNTER_CONTRACTS.md sec7.2). The same readout primitive `reveal` above uses (`stronghold_climax.gd::_place_readout`, now built from any config entry rather than only `reveal`), stood at band 5's waystop instead of the arena threshold -- the owner's Sec10 readiness layer in the world, so the player learns the garrison's numbers before committing to the final approach. No `mark`: the waystop is band 5's own clearing, outside the stronghold's marker set, so `fallback` is the only coordinate this entry has. [-25.0, 7466.0] sits 9.9m from the waystop's own fire ((-22.6,7456.4), data/config/bands/band5_stronghold_approach/props.json) almost exactly on the bearing from that fire to the Hall (outer_works, world (8,7560)) -- in frame as the player leaves camp for the works, per R-2's own fail condition -- and 5m clear of the northmost camp prop (the crate at (-22.6,7461.0)), so it stands in the open rather than inside the furniture cluster. Carries no flag and gates nothing: reading it is optional, same as the reveal, and the text only ever gives the draw -- `tests/test_dialogue_runner.gd`'s spoiler scan forbids naming what is in chamber five here.
_comment_warden: R8.3. He is an ORDINARY row of data/config/trainers.json -- same table, same team schema, same reward schema, same defeat flag, same encounter_director.begin_trainer_battle() -- carrying `placed_by: "stronghold_climax"` so the world's own trainer pass and the stronghold's gauntlet pass both skip him and this file's mark decides where he stands. There is no boss combat mode and there is no boss script: 'the hardest trainer in the chapter' is a team and a set of levels, which is exactly what Sec12 asks for.
_comment_legendary: R8.4. CLAUDE.md's hard rule, restated so nobody has to go looking: no new creature meshes for the Meadows at any credit balance. `veridian` is already in data/creatures/species.json with real production art (board 06, owner-approved as the legendary's direct source), already the tallest body in the roster at 2.6m, and already has an OF28 `vivid` colourway. Everything below is the LEGAL differentiation on top of that one existing mesh: a scale multiplier that puts it a further half-metre over its own wild size, restraint VFX while it is bound and a release light when it is freed. No new model, no new generation, no repaint beyond the colourway system that already ships.
_comment_staging: OP-0904-8 (owner 2026-09-04: 'The legendary should be in the machine not in a ring outside the machine'). While bound it stands INSIDE the Tether Machine, in the cage void the board draws its prisoner in: on the machine's axis, above the dais the installed mesh carries there, under its crown. `stage` tunes how that void is MEASURED off the mesh (stronghold_climax.gd::_measure_cage), never where it is -- D49's lesson. On the installed mesh fitted to 15 m: dais 3.13 m, crown 8.89 m, void 5.76 m, 2.6 m of headroom over the 3.17 m creature. `mark`/`fallback` below are where the FREED creature steps out to (R8.2's `legendary_stand`, +6 m in the chamber's local depth), and where the bound one stands only when no stronghold is in the tree.

legendary._comment_level: Above the Warden's own team, which is the point -- this is what Team Tether was holding. TUNABLE.
legendary._comment_facing: Local to the stronghold's frame, like every other facing. 180 faces the chamber's -depth side: the reveal stand and the arch's face, so the player who walks round to look at it meets its eyes.
legendary._comment_scale: On top of the species' own 2.6m, so it stands ~3.2m in the chamber -- a head and a rack above anything else the player has met, and visibly not the same animal as a wild one would be if one ever spawned. Applied to the model pivot, so the collider and the fit are untouched.

stage._comment: How the cage void is read off the machine mesh. `axis_probe_radius` is how far from the axis still counts as 'the middle' when finding the dais top and the crown underside; `clearance` lifts the feet that far off the dais so the hooves do not z-fight it.
stage._comment_step_out: How far clear of the machine's MEASURED plinth the freed creature stands. R8.2's `legendary_stand` mark is 6 m from the chamber centre and the installed mesh's plinth reaches 5.98 m, so the mark as authored left the freed creature standing on the base -- measured at 2.0 m off the axis in smoke_gate_e_finale. The mark's bearing is kept; only its distance is corrected, so stronghold.json (another file's) is untouched.

bound._comment: While it is held in the machine: drained, clamped, lit by somebody else's light. Two cold teal restraint rings (palette.json's reserved Tether teal) tight on the body -- `rings` are heights as fractions of the body's own height, the radius is the species' gameplay radius plus `ring_clearance` -- plus a slow pulse so it reads as machinery working rather than as scenery. The old 24-bar floor ring of radius 3.4 m is gone: it was the ring outside the machine.
bound._comment_emission: NOT higher. Above ~1.2 the teal clips to white and the ring stops reading as the reserved colour at all -- the same ceiling stronghold_occupation.gd's work-lamp lens found at 2.4 and fixed at 1.15, and the same finding a blind judge returned on these rings at 2.2 ('unlit white primitives').

draw._comment: The draw made visible: a column of the reserved teal from the creature's back up to the machine's crown, plus a light where it lands. Answers the one thing two blind judges independently named -- 'nothing connects the creature to the structure, so the central premise is not rendered'. Emission keeps the same 1.15 ceiling as the rings; the radii taper UP so the column reads as being taken from the animal rather than shone onto it.

freed._comment: The instant it is loose: the cage colour is gone and the light is its OWN -- warm, wide, and brighter than the machine ever was. This is the only moment in the chapter lit by something that is not Team Tether. It then STEPS OUT of the machine to the `mark` over `step_out_seconds` (down off the dais, then across), turns to the player, and on the join offer crosses to `approach_distance` from them over `approach_seconds`.

_comment_machine: R8.2 builds the Tether Machine itself (its board is owner-supplied and it is one of D24's three hero objects). This block only says where the player pushes the button and what it says -- `machine_foot` is that file's own mark for the machine's base.
_comment_flags: Every flag this item introduces, in the order the climax sets them. `legendary_freed` is the one SG44 reads -- the world event is a SEPARATE item and this file must never try to run it; it only records, once, that the thing which causes it has happened.

flags._comment_legendary_settled: GATE-E. `legendary_joined` records that the freed creature ended up on the belt; this records only that the roster DECISION is over, which is a different fact and the one prompt 68's objective chain has to wait on. A player with five they will not give up may let the legendary walk away, and that is a finished ending rather than an unfinished objective -- see stronghold_climax.gd::_settle() for why the chain cannot key on `legendary_joined`.
flags._comment_gate: The machine refuses to be touched until the Warden has fallen. Sec28's order is not optional and this is the one place a player could otherwise walk around it -- the Legendary Chamber is through the Warden Arena, and a player who sprints past him would otherwise reach the machine with the boss still standing.
